chapters.title: Autonomy and execution
chapters.caption: A goal in plain English. The real model chooses actions; Chromium performs the work.

chapters.title: Reliability: observe, then retry
chapters.caption: The first save failed. The worker checked the ledger, retried, and verified the exact fields.

chapters.title: Verification: saved row and browser evidence
chapters.caption: The persisted record matches the source: X-101, USD 1,240.50, due 2026-10-31.

chapters.title: Generalization: a read-only task
chapters.caption: A different vendor and objective use the same engine. Reporting makes no ledger write.

chapters.title: Generalization: multiple documents
chapters.caption: The same worker records all Company X invoices instead of only the latest one.

chapters.title: Product thinking: approval before a high-value write
chapters.caption: Northstar's USD 7,800 record requires a human decision. The worker pauses before writing.

chapters.title: Reliability: uncertain acknowledgement
chapters.caption: The save commits but its acknowledgement is lost. Checking the ledger prevents a duplicate.

chapters.title: Reliability: bounded failure
chapters.caption: A permanent outage stops after three save attempts. No false completion claim is made.

chapters.title: Verification: reject corrupted persistence
chapters.caption: A corrupted amount fails exact-field verification. The conflicting record needs manual review.

chapters.title: Product thinking: ask instead of guessing
chapters.caption: A missing source due date stops the task. The worker does not invent a value.

chapters.title: Engineering quality and technical understanding
chapters.caption: A small planner, executor and verifier. Each component has one job; limitations are explicit.

chapters.title: Measured evaluation evidence
chapters.caption: Review real API and browser test results. These are observed results in a narrow sandbox, not a universal guarantee.
